Its steps 1.1–2.1 give M=L^T L, step 3.1 identifies d_M with the Euclidean feature distance, and step 4.1 proves the pseudometric axioms. The definition only promises this same-page theorem, not a proof in its own carrier; q_M is nonnegative under its PSD hypothesis, so its square root exists by thm-of-square-roots.

The supplier indexes entries by 0<=r,s<d while the lemma silently uses 1<=i,j<=d. This is a missing notation conversion, not a counterexample to the coordinate isometry: the order-preserving bijections i=r+1 and j=s+1 give identical entry lists and sums. Added the explicit convention A_ij=A(i-1,j-1) in the Statement and the finite reindexing identity in F1. At d=1 the sole coordinate A_11 is exactly A(0,0). The inverse, linearity, inner-product identity and norm identity are unchanged.
